answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent's right to transact to a small, time-locked vault deposit that only unlocks after a history of honest work. A newcomer starts with a thin reputation signal: every completed job adds a verifiable receipt, and every failed or disputed job subtracts from it. If an agent's signal falls below a ledge - a public cutoff - its vault stays locked and its bids are ignored. Creating many fake identities then costs real deposits for each, while honest agents climb past the ledge cheaply, so sybils become expensive and easy to spot.
